scope: Current published package regression; bounded VB6 Actor checkbox sample and self-owned dual-width VB fixture, not full VB5/VB6 acceptance.

real_actor.outcome: Two actual runtime-owned checkbox glyphs each match 182 original resource pixels; four BM_CLICK messages per checkbox restored original check state, font and style; child process exited and owned job was empty.

corrected_edit_test.result: Both own instances: a runtime-owned numeric textbox changed 0 to 2 via WM_SETTEXT, read back through WM_GETTEXT, restored to 0, and EM_GETSEL returned (0,1); process exited and owned job empty.
corrected_edit_test.prior_observer_error: The first probe used cross-process GetWindowTextW after mutation and falsely reported failure; preserved logs are not counted as application failures.
limitations: one numeric field
no physical input, IME or independent notification assertion

model_regression.note: These are self-owned fixtures; x64 models do not represent an actual 64-bit VB runtime.

known_timeout: The S31 intermittent VB child timeout did not recur in this run; cause remains unproven and TODO remains open.

real_madshow.outcome: Both owned instances produced the same 21 runtime-owned child classes, preserved selection in inventory mode, exited successfully and left no owned processes; current style DLL appeared only in styled instance. Images visibly differ, but this inventory does not establish per-control hook attachment or input behavior.
not_covered: individual control pixel and interaction changes

attachment_observer_attempt.method: Temporary self-owned x86 observer based on tests/integration/vb_intrinsic.c and vb_queue.c, targeted only at the newly launched instance UI thread.
attachment_observer_attempt.failure: WH_GETMESSAGE and WH_CALLWNDPROC SetWindowsHookExW returned NULL with ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND (126) before per-control survey. The controller successfully loaded the witness and resolved both exports.
attachment_observer_attempt.independent_control: An independently rebuilt same-source witness in task scratch also returned 126 for both hooks; no claim about renderer attachment follows.
attachment_observer_attempt.cleanup: Process exit closed its owned kill-on-close job; no existing process was targeted.
attachment_observer_attempt.unresolved: Underlying cause of 126 remains unproven; no renderer attachment conclusion follows.
attachment_observer_attempt.single_process_control: Correction: the same-thread vb-queue-test passed after setting hMod=NULL for the current-process hook procedure. Its earlier 126 with non-NULL module was an invalid same-thread control, and cannot be used to infer a general observer or environment failure. The original cross-process 126 remains unexplained.

instrumented_build.scope: Self-owned scratch-only copy of S63 source; adds one file trace immediately after install_created decides installed. Not a shipped DLL and not a direct query of the released DLL.
instrumented_build.build: x86 GCC C17 Ninja ccache; core/abi passed; diagnostic copy also built x64 but only x86 used for real VB6 sample
instrumented_build.matching: All 20 child HWND/class pairs from inventory matched installed=1 in trace; nonvisual ThunderRT6Timer did not appear in installation trace. Root ThunderRT6FormDC installed=1; hidden ThunderRT6Main installed=0.
instrumented_build.comparison: Complete diagnostic screenshot SHA-256 equals the earlier same-sample released DLL screenshot; this does not prove absence of all diagnostic effects.
limitations: instrumented test build, not production DLL introspection
physical input not covered
does not prove every visual state or all VB5/VB6 controls
cross-process observer failure remains unexplained

edit_interaction_attempt.scope: One runtime-owned editable ThunderRT6TextBox containing 0.1, in separate self-owned bare and released-package styled instances, DPI 96. No simulator buttons or disk operations.
edit_interaction_attempt.settext_control: WM_SETTEXT to 0.2 returned 0 and did not change the value in bare instance; setting original value returned 1. This was not tested against styled instance in that first control.
edit_interaction_attempt.char_control: In both bare (PID 12156) and styled (PID 5040), AttachThreadInput and SetFocus succeeded and EM_SETSEL/EM_GETSEL returned (2,3); synchronous WM_CHAR for 2 did not change the observed text. The original value remained 0.1 after the attempted restoration. Both tests reported failure rather than passing the intended interaction assertion.
edit_interaction_attempt.conclusion: The same behavior on bare and styled is not evidence of a style regression. Cause is undetermined; synthetic input is not a successful editing or notification test, and no physical keyboard claim is made.
edit_interaction_attempt.cleanup: Probe exited nonzero, closing its kill-on-close job; instances were self-owned.
edit_interaction_attempt.correction: Earlier value_ok=0 was read using GetWindowTextW from another process. Windows does not provide reliable cross-process control-text reads through GetWindowTextW; it is not proof that WM_CHAR failed or that the text remained unchanged. Both corrected probes read the control through WM_GETTEXT.

corrected_result.result: Both own instances: successful AttachThreadInput/SetFocus, EM_SETSEL and EM_GETSEL=(2,3), WM_CHAR produced 0.2 as read with WM_GETTEXT, WM_SETTEXT restored 0.1 as read with WM_GETTEXT, normal process exit and owned job empty.
limitations: one numeric field
synthetic WM_CHAR is not physical keyboard input
no independent notification count or IME
same-process application state beyond window text not independently checked

observer_text_fix.scope: Two cross-process VB observer control reads only: child inventory text and About button lookup; top-level window title retrieval and in-process vb6-probe were not changed.
observer_text_fix.problem: GetWindowTextW returns cached caption rather than querying an edit control in another process. Actor path control previously appeared empty; actual WM_GETTEXT reports O:\winnt.
observer_text_fix.implementation: SendMessageTimeoutW(WM_GETTEXT) with a 1000 ms bounded wait, initialized buffer, and explicit failure; user input and product renderer are unchanged.
observer_text_fix.regression: Self-owned isolated x86 and x64 cross-process EDIT controls set and read a Unicode string, reject invalid HWND and clean up. Modified old GetWindowTextW implementation failed on the expected string in both widths, exit 1; fixed version passed with legacy_equal=0.
observer_text_fix.final_real_actor: Fresh 32-bit Actor under installed assets DLL reports O:\winnt, 0 and 1 text values, 13 windows and job empty; log build/t18-s64-vbtext-final-actor/output.txt.
limits: One real VB6 app and x86 runtime; model x64 is not a 64-bit VB runtime
No physical keyboard, IME or independent notification assertion
Other optional observers and custom control protocols not covered

vb_queue_p2.scope: The self-owned same-thread vb-queue unit fixture only; cross-process hook installation is a separate unresolved problem.
vb_queue_p2.old_result: Original S64 P1 x86 and x64 vb-queue-test each failed at hook installation with error 126, exit 1.
vb_queue_p2.fix: For callbacks targeting the current thread in the current process, pass NULL hMod while keeping the callback DLL loaded and explicitly freeing it after unhook.
vb_queue_p2.verified: x86 and x64 queue tests passed, including wrong tag rejection, notification and post-unhook negative; clean package focused 14 cases in 11.37 seconds no skips; both installed launchers passed each architecture.
vb_queue_p2.cross_process_control: Separate x86 and x64 owned-process EDIT tests each failed to install WH_CALLWNDPROC with non-NULL DLL hMod and error 126. Controller and target were on the same private desktop; GetModuleHandleEx(FROM_ADDRESS) returned the supplied module. Cause remains undetermined; same-thread fix is not a solution.
limitations: No production renderer change
Does not establish real-app cross-process observer support
No VB5/VB6 full compatibility claim

real_intrinsic_p3.scope: Two independently compiled original x86 samples using actual runtime50/runtime60; original provenance and license in docs/history/M0-T17-S4-vb-intrinsics.md and evidence vb-intrinsic-controls.json. The samples are not required build dependencies.
real_intrinsic_p3.behavior: Option group, two-click checkbox cycles, combo selection and dropdown cancellation, list selection, text change and restoration, scrollbar public state; styled glyph pixel checks use project original resources.
limitations: Synthetic messages; no physical keyboard or IME verification
Selection and state are bounded to these sample variants and 96 DPI
No notification counts, real drag, direct replace/undo, full GDI lifetime, deferred OCX or DriveListBox proof
Only actual 32-bit VB runtimes; no 64-bit VB runtime claim

real_intrinsic_notifications_p4.scope: Self-owned test-only instrumentation of the existing renderer subclass in actual x86 VB5/VB6 samples; P2 release DLL was not modified. Each BEFORE and AFTER surrounds DefSubclassProc for WM_COMMAND with a VB runtime-owned child.
limitations: Counts cover full observed lifetime including setup, not only intentional input
Matched before/after does not independently prove the VB application event handler executed
Synthetic messages, not physical keyboard or mouse; scroll/list notifications and IME unverified
One VB5 diagnostic screenshot differed by 12676 bytes; one diagnostic and release repeat matched, cause remains unknown
VB6 screenshot matches prior release screenshot byte-for-byte
Diagnostic code is not a shipped binary; observation may perturb timing

vb5_screenshot_followup.same_size_headers: 579534 bytes, identical 54-byte BMP headers, 12676 differing bytes in pixel payload
vb5_screenshot_followup.interpretation: A single release and diagnostic repeat matched each other and original release screenshot; the first diagnostic outlier was not reproduced. Cause remains unknown; this does not establish absence of visual effects.

real_disabled_p5.scope: Actual x86 VB5/VB6 intrinsic samples at DPI 96; two bare and two styled processes, no external controls. Enabled state, font, window style and check/selection were restored after programmatic disable/reenable. Styled glyphs match original project resources.
false_starts: The initial test incorrectly expected EnableWindow(FALSE) to return nonzero for a previously enabled window; all four controls aborted before useful validation.
Sending BM_CLICK explicitly to disabled controls changed check state in bare and styled samples; it is not equivalent to a user clicking a disabled control and was removed from the final scenario.
The initial expectation that bare PrintWindow must differ for every disabled control failed in both baselines; final bare runs report differences but do not assert them.
limitations: Programmatic EnableWindow and PrintWindow, not physical mouse/keyboard
No actual disabled click, focus traversal, accessibility, IME or application notification assertions
One runtime version and DPI per sample; no OCX, DriveListBox or third-party variants
Does not establish that every pixel of disabled label matches Windows 3.x
